For an intimate event, workshop, or executive meeting of **20–40 guests** in Midtown Manhattan / Times Square, you generally want to avoid massive convention hotels where smaller groups get lost. Instead, boutique and lifestyle hotels offer dedicated, high-touch spaces with great tech and food options.

Here are the top hotel recommendations in that area categorized by vibe and style:

---

### 1. Modern & Flexible (Best for Workshops, Tech Meetings, Creative Brainstorms)

*   **Arlo Midtown** *(38th St between 8th & 9th Ave)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Sleek, modern, and design-forward.
    *   **Meeting Space:** Offers flexible **Studio spaces (Studios A, B, & C)** that can be used individually for 20–30 people or combined for up to 50–60. 
    *   **Why it works:** Dedicated built-in A/V, tons of natural light, and a stylish rooftop (ART Midtown) perfect for post-meeting drinks.

*   **AC Hotel New York Times Square** *(40th St between 7th & 8th Ave)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Sleek European minimalism, efficient, and corporate-friendly.
    *   **Meeting Space:** The **AC Meeting Rooms** hold around 20–30 in classroom/boardroom setups or up to 40 in a reception style.
    *   **Why it works:** Great plug-and-play tech, excellent coffee breaks, and just far enough off 7th Ave to avoid heavy pedestrian traffic while being steps from Times Square.

---

### 2. Luxury Boutique (Best for C-Level Board Meetings & VIP Dinners)

*   **The Chatwal, New York** *(44th St between 5th & 6th Ave)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Art Deco luxury, private, and highly personalized service.
    *   **Meeting Space:** **The Stanford White Studio** or **The Landmark Room** are perfect for 15–30 guests in a boardroom setup or up to 40 for a cocktail reception.
    *   **Why it works:** Located on a quieter block near the Theater District. Offers high-end catering by Lambs Club and top-tier confidentiality/service.

*   **The Knickerbocker Hotel** *(42nd St & Broadway)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Historic luxury meets modern chic right on the corner of Times Square.
    *   **Meeting Space:** Private event rooms and semi-private spaces at **Charlie Palmer at The Knick**, ideal for 20–40 guests for private dining or seated presentations.
    *   **Why it works:** Unbeatable location, high-end catering, and access to **St. Cloud**, one of the best rooftops overlooking Times Square.

---

### 3. Contemporary & High-Floor Views (Best for Presentations & Receptions)

*   **Hyatt Centric Times Square New York** *(45th St between 6th & 7th Ave)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Upscale, vibrant, and centrally located.
    *   **Meeting Space:** **T45 Meeting Rooms** offer flexible configurations suitable for 20–40 guests (classroom, theater, or boardroom).
    *   **Why it works:** Offers natural light, modern A/V setups, and you can cap off the day at **Bar 54**, one of the highest open-air hotel rooftop lounges in NYC.

*   **Archer Hotel New York** *(38th St between 5th & 6th Ave)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Industrial-chic boutique with a cozy, upscale feel.
    *   **Meeting Space:** The private dining space at **AKB (Archer's Kitchen & Bar)** or private foyer spaces can easily accommodate intimate groups of 20–30.
    *   **Why it works:** Just a short walk to Times Square, Bryant Park, and Grand Central. Features **Spyglass Rooftop Bar** with direct views of the Empire State Building.

---

### Quick Comparison Summary

| Hotel | Vibe | Best Group Size | Key Highlight |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Arlo Midtown** | Creative / Modern | 20–40 pax | Built-in A/V, modular rooms |
| **AC Hotel Times Square** | Efficient / Corporate | 20–30 pax | Minimalist design, clean tech |
| **The Chatwal** | High-End Luxury | 15–30 pax | Luxury service, Art Deco style |
| **The Knickerbocker** | Iconic / Upscale | 20–40 pax | Prime location, St. Cloud rooftop |
| **Hyatt Centric** | Modern / High Views | 20–40 pax | Great light, Bar 54 access |

### Tips for Booking Small Meetings in Midtown:
1. **F&B Minimums:** Most of these hotels will charge a Food & Beverage (F&B) minimum rather than just a room rental fee, especially if you order breakfast/lunch catering.
2. **A/V Requirements:** Ask if A/V is included in the room package. Boutique properties like *Arlo* and *AC Hotel* often have built-in screens/monitors, saving you thousands on third-party A/V vendors.
3. **Subway Access:** If your guests are local commuters, hotels near 42nd St (Knickerbocker, Hyatt Centric) or 38th St (Arlo, Archer) offer fast access to the N/Q/R/W, 1/2/3, 7, and A/C/E lines.

For an unforgettable Broadway date night, you want a hotel that strikes the perfect balance: close enough to walk to the theater (so you aren’t stressing in Midtown traffic), romantic, and home to a stunning rooftop bar for pre-show drinks or a nightcap.

Here are the best hotels in NYC that fit this exact vibe, tailored by style:

---

### 1. The Theater-Lover’s Dream: **CIVILIAN Hotel**
* **Neighborhood:** Hell’s Kitchen / Theater District (48th St)
* **The Rooftop:** **Starchild Rooftop**
* **The Vibe:** Trendy, boutique, and stylishly homage-driven.
* **Why it’s perfect:** Designed by David Rockwell, this hotel is literally a love letter to Broadway, featuring theater memorabilia and costume sketches throughout. It’s steps from most theaters. Afterwards, head up to **Starchild**, a cozy lounge with a retractable roof, great cocktails, and brilliant views of the West Side skyline.

### 2. Luxury & Sexy: **The Times Square EDITION**
* **Neighborhood:** Times Square (7th Ave & 47th St)
* **The Rooftop:** **The Terrace & Outdoor Gardens**
* **The Vibe:** Upscale, lush, and sophisticated.
* **Why it’s perfect:** Don't let the Times Square address scare you away—once you step inside, it feels like an oasis. The hotel is ultra-chic and romantic. Their restaurant and outdoor terrace (curated by Michelin-starred chef John Fraser) feels like a secret garden suspended above the chaotic city below. 

### 3. The Classic Romantic with Iconic Views: **Archer Hotel New York**
* **Neighborhood:** Midtown South / Bryant Park (38th St)
* **The Rooftop:** **Spyglass Rooftop Bar**
* **The Vibe:** Vintage glamour, intimate, and upscale.
* **Why it’s perfect:** Located about a 10-to-12-minute walk from the heart of Broadway, the Archer offers a quieter, more sophisticated escape. The crown jewel is **Spyglass**, an 18th-floor rooftop with an up-close, unobstructed view of the Empire State Building. It’s hard to beat for a romantic nightcap.

### 4. Rustic Chic & Weather-Proof: **Refinery Hotel**
* **Neighborhood:** Midtown West (38th St)
* **The Rooftop:** **Refinery Rooftop**
* **The Vibe:** Industrial-chic, lively, and stylish.
* **Why it’s perfect:** A converted garment factory turned boutique hotel. It’s a short walk or quick cab to the theaters. The rooftop has a retractable glass roof, brick walls, and fairy lights, making it ideal **regardless of the weather**. It’s consistently rated one of the best rooftop bars in Midtown.

### 5. Historic Glamour: **The Knickerbocker Hotel**
* **Neighborhood:** Times Square / 42nd Street
* **The Rooftop:** **St. Cloud Rooftop**
* **The Vibe:** Modern luxury inside a landmark luxury building.
* **Why it’s perfect:** Supposedly the birthplace of the martini, The Knickerbocker is right on the edge of Times Square. You can literally walk out the door to your show. **St. Cloud** sits on the roof, offering cozy corner "sky pods" looking directly over the lights of the city. 

---

### 💡 Pro-Tips for Your Date Night:

1. **Book Rooftop Reservations early:** Even if you are staying at the hotel, rooftop bars in Midtown get notoriously busy. Book a table for drinks 1.5 to 2 hours *before* your show, or make a reservation for right after the curtain calls (around 10:00–10:30 PM).
2. **Timing Your Dinner:** Most Broadway shows start at **7:00 PM or 8:00 PM**. If you want a full dinner, do a 5:00 PM dinner, show at 7:30 PM, and rooftop cocktails at 10:00 PM for the ultimate romantic finish.
3. **Pedi-Cabs over Taxis:** If you're wearing heels and don't want to walk 10 blocks after the show, skip the Ubers/Taxis (which will be stuck in gridlock) and grab a fun pedicab back to your hotel.

Because Times Square is the neon-lit heart of NYC’s Theater District and a major transit hub, the "best" hotel depends on the exact vibe you want for nightlife and culture. 

Here are the top picks, categorized by what kind of experience you are looking for:

---

### 1. Overall Best for Nightlife & High Culture: **The Times Square EDITION**
If you want luxury, high-end nightlife, and sleek culture without stepping foot outside your hotel, this is the premier choice. Designed by boutique hotel pioneer Ian Schrager, it offers a sophisticated escape from the chaotic streets below.
* **The Nightlife Scene:** It houses **Paradise Club**, a trendy nightlife venue and cabaret with performance art, DJs, and dancing. It also features **The Roof**, a lush, outdoor dining and cocktail space.
* **Culture Access:** Steps from top Broadway theaters, MoMA (Museum of Modern Art), and Rockefeller Center. 
* **Vibe:** Chic, luxurious, photo-worthy, and high-energy.

### 2. Best for Theater, Arts & Local Culture: **Civilian Hotel**
Tucked on 48th Street just off the main drag, Civilian was designed specifically as a love letter to Broadway and NYC theater culture. 
* **The Culture Scene:** The hotel’s decor features over 350 pieces of original theater art, props, and costume sketches. The ground-floor restaurant, **Rosevale Kitchen**, and the piano lounge feel like an insider hangout for Broadway actors and creatives.
* **The Nightlife Scene:** **Starchild Rooftop Bar** features a retractable roof, panoramic city views, and DJ sets late into the night.
* **Vibe:** Boutique, artistic, stylish, and deeply connected to NYC’s performing arts.

### 3. Best for Party Nightlife & Social Buzz: **Moxy NYC Times Square**
If your priority is high-energy partying, social scenes, and a youthful vibe, the Moxy is hard to beat.
* **The Nightlife Scene:** Home to **Magic Hour Rooftop Bar & Lounge**, one of the largest and most famous rooftops in the city. It features an adult "amusement park" theme, rotating seasonal pop-up installations, multiple bars, and top DJs.
* **Culture Access:** Located near the southern edge of Times Square, making it an easy walk down to the nightlife hubs of Chelsea and the Meatpacking District.
* **Vibe:** Trendy, energetic, fun, with smaller "micro-style" rooms meant mostly for sleeping after a long night out.

### 4. Best Historic NYC Vibe with Top-Tier Views: **The Knickerbocker Hotel**
Located directly on the corner of 42nd and Broadway, this is a historic landmark hotel (supposedly the birthplace of the Martini) restored into a modern luxury stay.
* **The Nightlife Scene:** **St. Cloud Rooftop** sits right over Times Square, offering one of the best elevated craft cocktail experiences in Midtown, surrounded by the glow of the billboards.
* **Culture Access:** Directly across from Bryant Park (host to seasonal cultural events and film screenings) and steps from the historic New York Public Library Main Branch.
* **Vibe:** Upscale, historic, refined, and classy.

---

### Pro-Tips for Nightlife & Culture in/around Times Square:

* **Jazz & Speakeasies Nearby:** Skip the generic tourist bars. Walk to **Birdland Jazz Club** (44th St) or **Iridium** for legendary music, or hunt down **Nothing Really Matters**, a hidden speakeasy tucked inside the 50th St subway station entrance.
* **Late-Night Food:** Head to **Hell’s Kitchen** (just west of Times Square along 9th Avenue) for incredible late-night dining, gay nightlife, and local bars that stay open until 4:00 AM.
* **Subway Advantage:** Times Square (42nd St station) is the biggest transit hub in the city. You can catch the **N/Q/R/W, 1/2/3, or A/C/E** trains directly down to the **Lower East Side, Greenwich Village, or Williamsburg (Brooklyn)** in under 20 minutes for NYC's indie music, subterranean clubs, and late-night food scenes.

evidence.aiResponse:
Assuming you mean **Midtown Manhattan, New York City**, the key to the ultimate food-and-theater trip is staying somewhere that offers luxury and peace, while placing you within a 5-to-15-minute walk of the Theater District and the city's best fine dining (avoiding tourist-trap restaurants).

Here are the top upscale hotels in Midtown tailored specifically for a food and theater lover, categorized by style:

---

### 1. The Chatwal, a Luxury Collection Hotel (Midtown West / Theater District)
* **The Vibe:** 1930s Art Deco glamour, intimate, and deeply connected to Broadway history.
* **Why it’s perfect for Theater:** It is literally located on 44th Street, in the heart of the Theater District. You can walk to almost any Broadway show in under 5 minutes. The hotel itself was originally the Lambs Club, America’s first professional theater club.
* **The Food Factor:** 
  * **On-site:** *The Lambs Club*, a classic, elevated American tavern with a stunning red-leather mezzanine and pre-theater tasting menus.
  * **Nearby:** You are steps from **Gabriel Kreuther** (2-Michelin-starred Alsatian fine dining) and **Aldo Sohm Wine Bar**.
* **Bonus:** Their concierge team is legendary for securing sold-out Broadway tickets and hard-to-get pre-theater reservations.

---

### 2. The Whitby Hotel (Upper Midtown / 56th St)
* **The Vibe:** Vibrant, British-chic luxury designed by Kit Kemp. Colorful, art-filled, and incredibly refined.
* **Why it’s perfect for Theater:** Located on 56th St between 5th and 6th Ave, it sits just north of the Theater District chaos. It’s an easy 10-minute stroll to the theaters, giving you a quiet sanctuary to return to after the curtain falls.
* **The Food Factor:** 
  * **On-site:** *The Whitby Bar & Restaurant* is a stylish spot for afternoon tea, craft cocktails, and high-end seasonal dining.
  * **Nearby:** You are a 5-minute walk from **Le Bernardin** (3 Michelin stars, arguably the best seafood in NYC) and **Marea** (upscale coastal Italian near Central Park).

---

### 3. The Times Square EDITION (7th Ave & 47th St)
* **The Vibe:** Sleek, modern, trendy luxury. An oasis of calm floating high above the lights of Times Square.
* **Why it’s perfect for Theater:** Ground zero for Broadway. You can look down at the theater lights from your floor-to-ceiling room windows and walk to your show in 2 minutes. 
* **The Food Factor:** 
  * **On-site:** Partnered with Michelin-starred Chef John Fraser. It features **701 West**, a sophisticated, fine-dining vegetable- and protein-forward restaurant, and **The Terrace**, an airy, lush indoor/outdoor spot perfect for a light bite or post-theater cocktail.
  * **Nearby:** Walkable to **Urban Hawker** (Singaporean street food market for a casual, high-quality lunch) and **L'Ami Pierre** for quick pre-show pastries/café bites.

---

### 4. The Knickerbocker Hotel (42nd St & Broadway)
* **The Vibe:** Historic Beaux-Arts luxury with a storied past (legend says the Martini was invented here). 
* **Why it’s perfect for Theater:** Overlooking Bryant Park and Times Square, it puts you right at the southern edge of the Theater District, seconds from *Harry Potter and the Cursed Child* and *Hamilton*.
* **The Food Factor:** 
  * **On-site:** Features dining curated by Master Chef Charlie Palmer, including **St. Cloud**, one of the absolute best upscale rooftop bars in Midtown for post-theater nightcaps.
  * **Nearby:** A short walk to **Ci Siamo** (Danny Meyer’s stellar Italian spot in Manhattan West) and **Sushi Amane**.

---

### 5. Baccarat Hotel New York (53rd St off 5th Ave)
* **The Vibe:** Ultra-luxury, opulent, drenched in Baccarat crystal, highly sensory and romantic.
* **Why it’s perfect for Theater:** Located near MoMA, it’s a 10-minute walk to the theaters. It offers a 5-star palatial retreat if you want to completely escape the theater crowds when the show is over.
* **The Food Factor:** 
  * **On-site:** **The Grand Salon** offers elevated French-inspired dining, a caviar menu, and standard-setting craft cocktails served in custom Baccarat glassware.
  * **Nearby:** A stone’s throw from **The Modern** (2 Michelin stars inside MoMA) and **Quality Bistro**.

---

### Quick Recommendation Summary:
* Choose **The Chatwal** if you want to be *on* the theater block with classic 1920s NYC charm.
* Choose **The Whitby** if you prioritize world-class boutique design and fine dining over being right in Times Square.
* Choose **The Times Square EDITION** if you want modern luxury, nightlife, and elevated food right in the center of the action. 

**Pro-Tip for Food & Theater:** NYC pre-theater dining hours (5:00 PM – 6:30 PM) book up months in advance. Once you pick your hotel, ask their concierge immediately to cross-reference your show times with reservations at nearby top-tier spots!

* **Why it’s perfect for Theater:** It is literally located on 44th Street, in the heart of the Theater District. You can walk to almost any Broadway show in under 5 minutes. The hotel itself was originally the Lambs Club, America’s first professional theater club.
* **The Food Factor:** 
  * **On-site:** *The Lambs Club*, a classic, elevated American tavern with a stunning red-leather mezzanine and pre-theater tasting menus.
  * **Nearby:** You are steps from **Gabriel Kreuther** (2-Michelin-starred Alsatian fine dining) and **Aldo Sohm Wine Bar**.
* **Bonus:** Their concierge team is legendary for securing sold-out Broadway tickets and hard-to-get pre-theater reservations.

---

### 2. The Whitby Hotel (Upper Midtown / 56th St)
* **The Vibe:** Vibrant, British-chic luxury designed by Kit Kemp. Colorful, art-filled, and incredibly refined.
* **Why it’s perfect for Theater:** Located on 56th St between 5th and 6th Ave, it sits just north of the Theater District chaos. It’s an easy 10-minute stroll to the theaters, giving you a quiet sanctuary to return to after the curtain falls.
* **The Food Factor:** 
  * **On-site:** *The Whitby Bar & Restaurant* is a stylish spot for afternoon tea, craft cocktails, and high-end seasonal dining.
  * **Nearby:** You are a 5-minute walk from **Le Bernardin** (3 Michelin stars, arguably the best seafood in NYC) and **Marea** (upscale coastal Italian near Central Park).

---

### 3. The Times Square EDITION (7th Ave & 47th St)
* **The Vibe:** Sleek, modern, trendy luxury. An oasis of calm floating high above the lights of Times Square.
* **Why it’s perfect for Theater:** Ground zero for Broadway. You can look down at the theater lights from your floor-to-ceiling room windows and walk to your show in 2 minutes. 
* **The Food Factor:** 
  * **On-site:** Partnered with Michelin-starred Chef John Fraser. It features **701 West**, a sophisticated, fine-dining vegetable- and protein-forward restaurant, and **The Terrace**, an airy, lush indoor/outdoor spot perfect for a light bite or post-theater cocktail.
  * **Nearby:** Walkable to **Urban Hawker** (Singaporean street food market for a casual, high-quality lunch) and **L'Ami Pierre** for quick pre-show pastries/café bites.

---

### 4. The Knickerbocker Hotel (42nd St & Broadway)
* **The Vibe:** Historic Beaux-Arts luxury with a storied past (legend says the Martini was invented here). 
* **Why it’s perfect for Theater:** Overlooking Bryant Park and Times Square, it puts you right at the southern edge of the Theater District, seconds from *Harry Potter and the Cursed Child* and *Hamilton*.
* **The Food Factor:** 
  * **On-site:** Features dining curated by Master Chef Charlie Palmer, including **St. Cloud**, one of the absolute best upscale rooftop bars in Midtown for post-theater nightcaps.
  * **Nearby:** A short walk to **Ci Siamo** (Danny Meyer’s stellar Italian spot in Manhattan West) and **Sushi Amane**.

---

### 5. Baccarat Hotel New York (53rd St off 5th Ave)
* **The Vibe:** Ultra-luxury, opulent, drenched in Baccarat crystal, highly sensory and romantic.
* **Why it’s perfect for Theater:** Located near MoMA, it’s a 10-minute walk to the theaters. It offers a 5-star palatial retreat if you want to completely escape the theater crowds when the show is over.
* **The Food Factor:** 
  * **On-site:** **The Grand Salon** offers elevated French-inspired dining, a caviar menu, and standard-setting craft cocktails served in custom Baccarat glassware.
  * **Nearby:** A stone’s throw from **The Modern** (2 Michelin stars inside MoMA) and **Quality Bistro**.

---

### Quick Recommendation Summary:
* Choose **The Chatwal** if you want to be *on* the theater block with classic 1920s NYC charm.
* Choose **The Whitby** if you prioritize world-class boutique design and fine dining over being right in Times Square.
* Choose **The Times Square EDITION** if you want modern luxury, nightlife, and elevated food right in the center of the action. 

**Pro-Tip for Food & Theater:** NYC pre-theater dining hours (5:00 PM – 6:30 PM) book up months in advance. Once you pick your hotel, ask their concierge immediately to cross-reference your show times with reservations at nearby top-tier spots!

When selecting the best full-service hotel near Times Square with meeting rooms, the right choice depends on the **size of your event** and the **vibe** you want. Times Square offers everything from massive convention hotels to sophisticated luxury properties just steps away from the noise.

Here are the top recommendations, categorized by what they do best:

---

### 1. The Undisputed Best Overall for Meetings: **New York Marriott Marquis**
* **Location:** 1535 Broadway (Right in the heart of Times Square)
* **Best For:** Large conferences, trade shows, and all-in-one convenience.

**Why it’s great:** 
The Marriott Marquis is a massive, iconic full-service flagship property designed specifically to handle events. It boasts over **100,000 square feet** of flexible event space across 40+ meeting rooms, including the Broadway Ballroom (which can hold up to 2,800 people).

* **Full-Service Amenities:** 24-hour fitness center, multiple on-site dining options (including *Le Broadway Cabaret* and the newly renovated *Broadway Lounge* with views of Times Square), in-room dining, dedicated event planners, and on-site AV teams.
* **Meeting Features:** State-of-the-art hybrid meeting technology, customizable catering, and direct elevator access to dedicated meeting floors.

---

### 2. Best for Luxury & Executive Meetings: **InterContinental New York Times Square**
* **Location:** 300 W 44th St (1 block west of Times Square)
* **Best For:** High-end corporate retreats, board meetings, and upscale gatherings.

**Why it’s great:** 
Located on 44th Street and 8th Avenue, it’s close enough to walk to Times Square in two minutes, but far enough to escape the immediate pedestrian traffic. It offers a refined, quiet atmosphere with luxury-tier service.

* **Full-Service Amenities:** Concierge lounge, upscale dining at *The Starlite Cocktails & Dining*, 24-hour room service, luxury sedan services, and floor-to-ceiling windows in room options.
* **Meeting Features:** **13,000 square feet** of meeting space across 13 rooms, including the Gotham Ballroom. Many meeting rooms feature natural sunlight—a rarity in Midtown Manhattan hotels.

---

### 3. Best for Mid-Sized Business Events & Wellness: **The Westin New York at Times Square**
* **Location:** 270 W 43rd St (At 8th Ave)
* **Best For:** Mid-sized corporate meetings, multi-day seminars, and business travelers.

**Why it’s great:** 
Connected directly to the E-Walk complex, the Westin balances business efficiency with guest comfort. It features Westin’s signature focus on wellness (Heavenly Beds, gear lending for workouts).

* **Full-Service Amenities:** *Foundry Kitchen & Bar*, 24-hour room service, expansive WestinWORKOUT Fitness Studio, concierge, and valet parking.
* **Meeting Features:** **34,000 square feet** of event space, including 32 meeting rooms and a 13-screen movie theater complex adjacent to the property (available for unique presentations or keynotes).

---

### 4. Best for Quiet, High-End Luxury Just Off-Square: **Sofitel New York**
* **Location:** 45 W 44th St (Between 5th & 6th Aves – 2 blocks east of Times Square)
* **Best For:** Executive board meetings, international guests, and intimate corporate dinners.

**Why it’s great:** 
If you want to be *near* Times Square without feeling like you are in the middle of it, the Sofitel is ideal. It brings a French chic, diplomatic level of service and a much calmer street environment.

* **Full-Service Amenities:** *Gaby Brasserie Française*, 24/7 room service, dedicated concierge team, fitness center, and pet-friendly luxury services.
* **Meeting Features:** **6,700 square feet** of meeting space, including a stunning Paris Ballroom and stylish private boardrooms equipped with high-end tech and gourmet French catering options.

---

### 5. Best Boutique Luxury Pick: **The Knickerbocker Hotel**
* **Location:** 6 St. James Pl / 142 W 42nd St (Overlooking Times Square)
* **Best For:** Small executive meetings, VIP receptions, and high-impact pitch sessions.

**Why it’s great:** 
A historic landmark that was transformed into a modern luxury boutique hotel. It features one of the best rooftop bars in NYC (*St. Cloud*) overlooking Times Square.

* **Full-Service Amenities:** High-end dining curated by top chefs, priority access to rooftop events, luxury room amenities, 24-hour room service, and personalized concierge.
* **Meeting Features:** Smaller footprint compared to the Marriott (around 2,200 sq. ft. of indoor space), but offers high-end, customizable executive boardrooms and private dining spaces for VIP events.

---

### Quick Recommendation Guide:

* **Go with Marriott Marquis** if you have **100+ guests** or need turnkey, massive event infrastructure.
* **Go with InterContinental** if you want **upscale, quiet luxury** right next to the theater district.
* **Go with Westin** if you want a **classic corporate hotel** with great tech and mid-sized room configurations.
* **Go with Sofitel** if you prefer a **sophisticated, quiet retreat** 5 minutes from Times Square.

When traveling for business and needing proximity to both **Penn Station** (for Amtrak/LIRR/NJ Transit) and **Times Square** (for corporate headquarters and central subways), the ideal location is the **Midtown West / Garment District corridor (33rd St to 40th St, between 5th and 9th Avenues)**. 

Staying slightly *outside* the immediate chaos of Times Square offers a quieter, more upscale experience while keeping both hubs within a 5- to 10-minute walk.

Here are the top upscale hotels for business travelers in that exact zone, categorized by style:

---

### 1. Ultra-Modern & Closest to Penn/Moynihan: **Pendry Manhattan West**
* **Location:** 385 9th Ave (33rd St)
* **Distance:** 2-minute walk to Penn Station (Moynihan Train Hall); 12-minute walk to Times Square.
* **Vibe:** Sleek, high-end, modern luxury.
* **Why it’s great for business:** 
  * It sits in the new Manhattan West development right across from the Moynihan Train Hall (the clean, modern side of Penn Station).
  * Exceptional room design with large work desks, state-of-the-art tech, and floor-to-ceiling windows.
  * Features high-end dining (Katsuya, Zou Zou’s) and upscale, quiet cocktail lounges perfect for meeting clients.
  * Quiet away from the street noise.

### 2. High-End Executive Classic: **The Langham, New York, Fifth Avenue**
* **Location:** 400 5th Ave (at 36th St)
* **Distance:** 8-minute walk to Penn Station; 8-minute walk to Times Square.
* **Vibe:** Refined, understated 5-star luxury.
* **Why it’s great for business:**
  * Some of the largest standard guest rooms in NYC, featuring massive marble bathrooms and spacious workspace setups.
  * Home to *Ai Fiori*, a Michelin-starred restaurant great for executive dinners.
  * Exceptional concierge service and smooth express check-ins.
  * Located on 5th Avenue, putting you equidistant from both locations while feeling distinctly premium.

### 3. Boutique & Efficient: **Archer Hotel New York**
* **Location:** 45 W 38th St (between 5th & 6th Ave)
* **Distance:** 7-minute walk to Times Square; 8-minute walk to Penn Station.
* **Vibe:** Industrial chic, polished, boutique upscale.
* **Why it’s great for business:**
  * Designed specifically with the discerning business traveler in mind—rooms feature ergonomic workspaces, Nespresso machines, and high-speed Wi-Fi.
  * Features *AKB*, a popular ground-floor bar for low-key meetings, and *Spyglass*, a rooftop bar with direct Empire State Building views for entertaining clients.
  * Tucked on a quieter side street, minimizing city noise.

### 4. Luxury on the Edge of Times Square: **The Knickerbocker Hotel**
* **Location:** 6 Rockefeller Plaza / 142 W 42nd St (at Broadway)
* **Distance:** Directly at Times Square; 10-minute walk (or 1 subway stop) to Penn Station.
* **Vibe:** Historic luxury meets modern minimalism.
* **Why it’s great for business:**
  * If you want to be *right* at Times Square without sacrificing sleep, this is the best option. The rooms feature heavy soundproofing and automated black-out drapes.
  * Features *St. Cloud*, a massive rooftop lounge ideal for hosting events or corporate drinks.
  * Direct access to the Times Square subway station beneath the building for rapid travel around the city.

### 5. Tech-Forward & Hyatt Loyalty: **Andaz 5th Avenue**
* **Location:** 485 5th Ave (at 41st St)
* **Distance:** 4-minute walk to Times Square; 12-minute walk to Penn Station.
* **Vibe:** Loft-style upscale, modern, relaxed.
* **Why it’s great for business:**
  * Located directly across from the New York Public Library, offering a sophisticated atmosphere.
  * Apartment-style rooms with massive ceilings, large desks, and complimentary non-alcoholic minibar snacks/drinks.
  * Excellent functional meeting spaces and hassle-free, app-based or host-assisted check-in.

---

### Quick Recommendation Summary:
* **Best overall for train travel (Amtrak/Penn):** *Pendry Manhattan West*
* **Best for high-level executives needing space:** *The Langham*
* **Best mid-sized boutique with great work setups:** *Archer Hotel*
* **Best if your meetings are strictly in Times Square:** *The Knickerbocker*

Assuming you are looking in **Midtown Manhattan (New York City)**, here are the top hotel rooftop recommendations tailored for a private celebration, categorized by the vibe and style of event you might be planning:

---

### 1. Best Overall & Weather-Proof: **Refinery Hotel** *(Refinery Rooftop)*
* **Vibe:** Industrial chic, warm, and lively with unobstructed views of the Empire State Building.
* **Why it’s great for a private celebration:** It features a **retractable glass roof**, meaning your event will go on rain or shine without sacrificing the view or outdoor feel. They offer dedicated event spaces, customizable catering menus, and excellent craft cocktails.
* **Best for:** Milestone birthdays, engagement parties, or corporate cocktail receptions (30–100+ guests).

### 2. Best for High Luxury & Sophistication: **The Peninsula New York** *(Salon de Ning)*
* **Vibe:** Glamorous, Asian-inspired lounge with a dramatic 1930s Shanghai feel and sweeping Fifth Avenue views.
* **Why it’s great for a private celebration:** It offers two outdoor terraces and an intimate interior lounge. It feels highly exclusive, with world-class five-star service and upscale small plates.
* **Best for:** Elegant anniversary parties, VIP dinners, or sophisticated cocktail soirées (Small to medium groups).

### 3. Best for Intimate Gatherings & Views: **Archer Hotel** *(Spyglass Rooftop Bar)*
* **Vibe:** Sophisticated, 1940s & 50s Glamour, intimate setting.
* **Why it’s great for a private celebration:** Located on the 22nd floor, Spyglass offers a front-row, direct view of the Empire State Building. Because the space is smaller than massive party rooftops, renting it out or reserving a dedicated section feels very private and exclusive.
* **Best for:** Intimate cocktail parties (20–60 guests) looking for iconic photo ops.

### 4. Best for High-Energy & Trendy Parties: **Moxy NYC Times Square** *(Magic Hour Rooftop Bar & Lounge)*
* **Vibe:** Playful, vibrant, "adult playground" with an amusement-park-inspired decor (including a mini-golf course).
* **Why it’s great for a private celebration:** It is Manhattan’s largest all-season hotel rooftop. It features multiple distinct areas (like the Foreplay mini-golf area, multiple bars, and outdoor terraces) that can be individually rented out for semi-private or full-buyout events.
* **Best for:** Lively birthday bashes, bachelorette parties, or dynamic celebrations with dancing and DJ setups.

### 5. Best for Modern Sleekness & VIP Spaces: **The Knickerbocker Hotel** *(St. Cloud Rooftop)*
* **Vibe:** Ultra-modern, sleek, and upscale right in the heart of Times Square.
* **Why it’s great for a private celebration:** St. Cloud features **three plush corner "sky pods"** that overlook Times Square. You can reserve one of these private pods for small groups, or opt for a full buyout of the venue for a larger-scale party.
* **Best for:** Medium-to-large private events that want a VIP, elevated nightlife atmosphere.

---

### Key Tips When Booking a Midtown Rooftop Event:
1. **Ask about Minimum Spend vs. Venue Fee:** Most Midtown hotel rooftops operate on a food-and-beverage minimum spend rather than a flat rental fee, especially for weeknight/weekend evening events.
2. **Weather Contingency:** If booking an outdoor-only rooftop, always ask if they have an indoor backup room or a retractable enclosure in case of rain/extreme cold.
3. **Sound Restrictions:** If you plan on having a live DJ or speeches, check the venue's decibel limits and audio capabilities.

***

**Would you like me to narrow these down based on your estimated guest count, target budget, or specific month/season?**

Hosting a bachelorette party in the Times Square area offers plenty of exciting options. Here are some ideas for venues and activities:

1. **Rooftop Bars**: Enjoy stunning views of New York City with cocktails at rooftop bars like The Skylark, Bar 54 at the Hyatt Centric Times Square, or St. Cloud at the Knickerbocker Hotel.

2. **Restaurants**: Book a fun group dinner at popular restaurants like Carmine’s for Italian family-style dining, Dos Caminos for Mexican cuisine, or Sushi by Bou for an intimate sushi experience.

3. **Broadway Shows**: Catch a Broadway show for an unforgettable night of entertainment. Be sure to book tickets in advance for popular shows.

4. **Karaoke**: Head to a karaoke bar like Karaoke Duet 35 or RPM Underground for a night of singing and dancing.

5. **Nightclubs**: Dance the night away at nearby clubs such as LAVO Nightclub or Marquee.

6. **Spa Day**: Start the day with relaxation at a spa like The Red Door by Elizabeth Arden or Haven Spa for massages and beauty treatments.

7. **Themed Tours**: Consider a themed walking tour or a party bus tour of the city to enjoy the sights with your friends.

8. **Hotel Suites**: Book a suite at a hotel like the Marriott Marquis or the W Times Square for a convenient and luxurious stay.

9. **Comedy Club**: Enjoy a night of laughter at a comedy club such as Carolines on Broadway.

10. **Private Event Spaces**: Rent a private room or event space at venues like 48 Lounge or The Press Lounge for a more personalized experience.

Remember to make reservations in advance, especially for larger groups, and check for any group packages or special bachelorette party offers.

To celebrate a graduation near Broadway, you’ll want a hotel that feels special, offers a great vibe for photos and dinners, and keeps you within easy walking distance of the theaters. 

Here are the top hotel recommendations near Broadway, categorized by the vibe you might be looking for:

---

### 1. Trendy & Celebration-Ready (Best for a fun, stylish vibe)

*   **The Times Square EDITION** *(701 7th Ave, right off Broadway)*
    *   **The Vibe:** High-end, modern, and energetic. 
    *   **Why it’s great for graduation:** It feels like a true luxury sanctuary hidden right in the middle of the excitement. It features **The Terrace and Outdoor Gardens** (a lush, green restaurant perfect for a celebratory dinner) and stylish cocktail lounges. The views of the city lights from the rooms are unmatched.
*   **Civilian Hotel** *(305 W 48th St, 1 block from Broadway)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Boutique, artsy, and deeply tied to Broadway theater culture.
    *   **Why it’s great for graduation:** Designed by David Rockwell, the hotel pays homage to Broadway history with theater props, costume sketches, and art throughout. It features **Starchild**, a fantastic rooftop lounge with a retractable roof, making it ideal for a celebratory drink after a show.

---

### 2. Best for Families & Groups (Spacious Rooms & Suites)

*   **Conrad New York Midtown** *(151 W 54th St, 2 blocks from Broadway)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Understated, quiet luxury. 
    *   **Why it’s great for graduation:** Unlike standard NYC hotel rooms, the Conrad offers **large, all-suite accommodations**. If parents, siblings, or grandparents are traveling together, the extra living space is a lifesaver. It’s located just north of the hectic core of Times Square, offering a more serene atmosphere while still being a 5-minute walk to Broadway theaters and Central Park.

---

### 3. Classic NYC Elegance (Best for a timeless, splurge-worthy feel)

*   **The Chatwal, a Luxury Collection Hotel** *(130 W 44th St, half a block from Broadway)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Historic 1930s Art Deco glam.
    *   **Why it’s great for graduation:** Nestled on a quieter side street in the heart of the Theater District, The Chatwal offers butler service, high-end dining at *The Lambs Club*, and an opulent, intimate feel. It feels like stepping into "Classic New York."
*   **The Knickerbocker Hotel** *(6 charged 42nd St & Broadway)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Sleek, historic luxury right on the corner of 42nd & Broadway.
    *   **Why it’s great for graduation:** It features **St. Cloud**, one of the best rooftops in Midtown with direct views over Times Square. It’s a great spot to toast the graduate at sunset before walking to an evening show.

---

### 4. Boutique & Great Value Luxury 

*   **Archer Hotel New York** *(45 W 38th St, near Broadway/Bryant Park)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Industrial-chic, charming, and attentive.
    *   **Why it’s great for graduation:** Located slightly south of Times Square near Bryant Park, it’s a quick walk to the Broadway theaters but in a slightly less congested area. The highlight is the **Spyglass Rooftop Bar**, which has incredible, up-close views of the Empire State Building—a fantastic backdrop for graduation photos.

---

### Tips for Planning a NYC Graduation Weekend:

1.  **Dining Reservations:** Midtown gets very busy around showtimes (5:00 PM – 7:00 PM). If you're planning a post-grad celebratory dinner, book **30 to 60 days in advance**. 
    *   *Great nearby spots:* **Ci Siamo** (Italian, nearby in Manhattan West), **The Meatball Shop** or **Joe Allen** (classic Theater District spots), or **Gallagher's Steakhouse** (for a traditional celebration).
2.  **Broadway Tickets:** If you are traveling with a group of 8 or more, look into group ticket sales through the official show sites to secure seats together. 
3.  **Photos:** Tell the hotel front desk in advance that you are celebrating a graduation—many properties will gladly send up a complimentary bottle of prosecco or a small treat to the room!

2.  **Broadway Tickets:** If you are traveling with a group of 8 or more, look into group ticket sales through the official show sites to secure seats together. 
3.  **Photos:** Tell the hotel front desk in advance that you are celebrating a graduation—many properties will gladly send up a complimentary bottle of prosecco or a small treat to the room!

Because Times Square is famously energetic, loud, and crowded, the key to a romantic stay here is finding a hotel that acts as a **luxurious, serene sanctuary** once you step inside, while still giving you easy access to Broadway and the iconic city lights.

Here are the best romantic hotels in (or immediately adjacent to) Times Square, ranked by vibe:

---

### 1. The Absolute Best Overall: **The Times Square EDITION**
* **Vibe:** Sleek, modern, sensual, and surprisingly serene.
* **Why it’s romantic:** Designed by legendary hotelier Ian Schrager, this hotel feels like a lush, elevated oasis floating above the chaos. It blends sleek, minimalist luxury with warm wood tones and tons of real greenery. 
* **Highlights:** 
  * **701West:** An incredible, romantic fine-dining restaurant led by a Michelin-starred chef.
  * **The Terraces:** Many rooms feature private outdoor terraces overlooking the city skyline—perfect for late-night champagne.
  * **Atmosphere:** Deep-soaking tubs, signature Le Labo scents tailored specifically for the hotel, and plush faux-fur throw blankets in the rooms.

---

### 2. Best for Old-Hollywood Glamour: **The Chatwal, A Luxury Collection Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Classic 1930s Art Deco, intimate, and deeply luxurious.
* **Why it’s romantic:** Located on 44th Street (just half a block from the heart of Times Square), The Chatwal offers an intimate, boutique feel that transports you back to the Golden Age of New York.
* **Highlights:**
  * **Butler Service:** Standard for many suites, making you feel pampered from arrival.
  * **The Lambs Club:** A stunning, cozy restaurant and lounge with a massive 1920s fireplace, perfect for pre-theater craft cocktails.
  * **Chatwal Spa:** Features private treatment rooms and an indoor plunge pool—a rarity in Mid-Town.

---

### 3. Best Iconic Views & Historic Charm: **The Knickerbocker Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Grand historic landmark meets modern luxury.
* **Why it’s romantic:** Sitting right on the corner of 42nd and Broadway, this host to 19th-century elite has been converted into a high-end luxury hotel. It offers custom soundproofing so you get the incredible views without any of the noise.
* **Highlights:**
  * **St. Cloud Rooftop:** One of the best rooftop bars in the city, offering private corner pods right above the Times Square lights. 
  * **Spacious Rooms:** High ceilings, massive windows, and luxurious stone bathrooms with rainfall showers.

---

### 4. Best Cozy Boutique Experience: **LUMA Hotel Times Square**
* **Vibe:** Modern, warm, attentive, and quiet.
* **Why it’s romantic:** Tucked away on 41st Street near Bryant Park, LUMA offers a quieter, more personal experience than the larger high-rises. It consistently ranks as one of the top-rated service hotels in NYC.
* **Highlights:**
  * **Aperitivo Hour:** Sangria and wine served in the lobby every evening.
  * **Azienda:** The superb in-house Basque tapas restaurant (Azienda) is dark, cozy, and perfect for date night.
  * **Floor-to-ceiling windows:** Roomy, brightly lit spaces with motorized blackout shades for sleeping in.

---

### 5. Best for Theater Lovers & Trendy Couples: **CIVILIAN Hotel**
* **Vibe:** Artsy, moody, theatrical, and stylish.
* **Why it’s romantic:** Designed by renowned architect David Rockwell, this hotel is a love letter to Broadway. It features dark blue velvet, brass accents, curating a sexy, dimly lit vibe throughout the property.
* **Highlights:**
  * **Starchild Rooftop:** Features a retractable glass roof, excellent cocktails, and sweeping city views.
  * **The Secret Garden:** A lush, hidden courtyard bar perfect for quiet conversations.

---

### Quick Recommendation Summary:
* Choose **The Times Square EDITION** if you want top-tier luxury, private outdoor balconies, and modern aesthetics.
* Choose **The Chatwal** if you want cozy, classic, high-end pampering with a spa.
* Choose **The Knickerbocker** if you want to be in the center of the action with an incredible rooftop.

**Pro-Tip for Booking:** Always request a **high floor** (20th floor or above) and ask for a room away from the elevators to ensure maximum quiet for your getaway!

For a Broadway-and-dining weekend, **stay in the West 40s or around Hell’s Kitchen**, ideally between **Eighth Avenue and Sixth Avenue**. You’ll be within an easy walk of most theaters, Restaurant Row, excellent pre-show dining, and late-night drinks—without needing a taxi or subway after the curtain call.[1][3]

## Best areas

- **Theater District / Times Square:** Best for convenience. Choose a hotel a few blocks west of Times Square if possible; you’ll remain close to Broadway while avoiding some of the busiest crowds.
- **Hell’s Kitchen:** Best overall balance for couples who prioritize restaurants and atmosphere. It’s a short walk to theaters and has a broad range of casual and upscale dining.
- **Bryant Park / west Midtown:** A slightly calmer, polished option with attractive hotels, easy theater access, and convenient subway connections.
- **SoHo or Greenwich Village:** Better for a romantic, neighborhood-focused weekend with standout dining, but expect a 15–25-minute taxi or subway ride to Broadway.

## Hotel picks

- **The Knickerbocker:** A polished choice directly by Times Square, with multiple dining and bar options and especially convenient theater access.[2]
- **W New York–Times Square:** Stylish and central, with Broadway essentially outside the door and an on-site restaurant.[4]
- **New York Marriott Marquis:** Best if you want a large full-service hotel in the heart of the Theater District, with its own dining and lounge options.[9]
- **Luma Hotel—Times Square:** A more intimate, modern option near Bryant Park and Broadway.
- **The Chatwal New York:** A quieter, more romantic luxury choice in the Theater District.
- **Soho Grand:** Choose this if dining, bars, and a more residential downtown feel matter more than being able to walk directly to the theater; it is in SoHo rather than Midtown.[8]

## Practical recommendation

For your specific weekend, choose **Hell’s Kitchen near West 46th–50th Streets** or **the quieter edge of Times Square near Sixth Avenue**. Reserve dinner for roughly **2½–3 hours before the show**, allowing time to eat, walk to the theater, and arrive 30–45 minutes before curtain.[3]

**Best default:** The Knickerbocker or Luma for maximum convenience; Hell’s Kitchen or SoHo for a more enjoyable dining-centered stay.

Finding a romantic hotel near Times Square and the Theater District can feel like a paradox: you want to be steps from Broadway, but you also want a serene, intimate sanctuary away from the neon lights and crowds. 

Fortunately, several upscale properties excel at creating a quiet, luxurious, and seductive atmosphere right in the heart of Midtown Manhattan. Below is a comparison of the top romantic upscale hotels in this area, categorized by their distinct romantic style.

---

### 1. The Chatwal, a Luxury Collection Hotel
**Best for:** Classic Gotham Glamour & Intimate Elegance  
**Location:** 44th Street (between 5th & 6th Aves) – *1 block from Theater District*

* **The Vibe:** 1930s Art Deco sophistication. Designed by famed architect Stanford White and restored by Thierry Despont, it feels like a private, high-society club from New York’s Golden Age.
* **Why it’s Romantic:** 
  * It is small and boutique (only 76 rooms), meaning personalized service, including custom butler service.
  * Deep red suede walls, leather accents, and retro-chic details create a sultry, cozy ambiance.
  * Features the **Chatwal Crown Spa**, offering intimate couple’s treatments and a private lap pool.
  * Suites feature private landscaped terraces—a rare luxury in Midtown.
* **Dining:** *The Lambs Club*, a dark-wood, fireplace-lit cocktail bar and restaurant perfect for pre- or post-theater drinks.

---

### 2. The Times Square EDITION

When looking for a family-friendly hotel in Times Square for a NYC vacation, there are several options that cater to families with amenities and conveniences. Here are a few highly regarded choices:

1. **The Westin New York at Times Square**: Known for its spacious rooms and central location, The Westin offers family-friendly amenities such as cribs and rollaway beds. It also features a fitness center and on-site dining options.

2. **Hilton Garden Inn Times Square**: This hotel is popular among families for its comfortable rooms and proximity to attractions. It offers amenities like free Wi-Fi, a mini-fridge, and a microwave in the room, which can be helpful for families with young children.

3. **The Knickerbocker Hotel**: A luxurious option with a historic touch, The Knickerbocker provides spacious rooms and suites. It offers family-friendly services and is located right in the heart of Times Square, making it convenient for exploring the city.

4. **Marriott Marquis Times Square**: This iconic hotel features large rooms that can accommodate families. The Marriott Marquis offers various dining options and an incredible view from its revolving restaurant, The View.

5. **Residence Inn New York Manhattan/Times Square**: Ideal for families who need a bit more space and kitchen facilities, the Residence Inn provides rooms with kitchenettes, complimentary breakfast, and a convenient location near Times Square.

6. **Element New York Times Square West**: An eco-friendly hotel that offers family-friendly suites with kitchenettes, free breakfast, and a rooftop patio. It’s a great choice for families looking for a modern and comfortable stay.

When choosing a hotel, consider the specific needs of your family, including room size, amenities, and proximity to attractions. Booking in advance can also help secure better rates and availability.

## Top Picks

### 🏆 **Marriott Marquis Times Square**
- **Why it works:** Central location, multiple room configurations, rooftop views
- **Highlights:** Large rooms, multiple dining options, revolving restaurant
- **Best for:** Families wanting everything in one place
- **Price range:** $$$-$$$$

### 🌟 **New York Hilton Midtown**
- **Why it works:** One of NYC's largest hotels, excellent accessibility
- **Highlights:** Connecting rooms available, reliable service, accessible for grandparents
- **Best for:** Large groups needing multiple rooms
- **Price range:** $$$

### 🏠 **Residence Inn by Marriott Times Square**
- **Why it works:** Suite-style rooms with kitchenettes
- **Highlights:** More space, ability to prepare some meals, cost-saving on dining
- **Best for:** Budget-conscious multigenerational groups
- **Price range:** $$-$$$

### ✨ **The Knickerbocker**
- **Why it works:** Boutique feel with great amenities
- **Highlights:** Rooftop bar, elegant rooms, excellent service
- **Best for:** Families wanting a more upscale experience
- **Price range:** $$$$

---

## Key Considerations for Multigenerational Travel

| Factor | What to Look For |
|--------|-----------------|
| **Accessibility** | Elevators, accessible rooms, proximity to transit |
| **Room options** | Suites, connecting rooms, multiple bed configs |
| **Dining** | On-site restaurants for varied tastes/schedules |
| **Location** | Close to attractions, manageable walking |
| **Amenities** | Pool, fitness center, concierge services |

---

## Practical Tips
- **Book connecting rooms early** — they sell out fast
- **Ask about rollaway beds** and crib availability
- **Consider 2 nearby rooms** vs. one suite for privacy
- **Look for hotels with 24-hour room service** for different sleep schedules

- 🍕 Classic NYC pizza spots

The "best" hotel near Times Square for an event depends on the size of your gathering, your budget, and the style you are looking for. 

Here are the top hotels near Times Square with outstanding ballrooms and meeting spaces, categorized by event type:

---

### 1. The Overall Best for Large Events & Scale: **New York Marriott Marquis**
If you need a massive, versatile space directly in the heart of Times Square, this is the undisputed leader.
* **Location:** 45th Street & Broadway (Directly in Times Square)
* **Total Meeting Space:** Over 100,000 sq. ft. across 40+ event rooms.
* **The Ballroom:** The **Broadway Ballroom** is one of the largest in NYC at nearly 29,000 sq. ft., capable of hosting up to 2,800 guests.
* **Why it’s the best:** It was built specifically for massive conventions, galas, and corporate events. It features state-of-the-art AV equipment, on-site event planners, direct elevators, and views overlooking Times Square.

### 2. Best High-End Luxury & Column-Free Space: **InterContinental New York Times Square**
For a sleeker, more sophisticated luxury experience that is just steps away from the noise of Times Square.
* **Location:** 44th Street & 8th Avenue (1 block west of Times Square)
* **Total Meeting Space:** 13,000 sq. ft. across 10 flexible meeting rooms.
* **The Ballroom:** The **Gotham Ballroom** (approx. 6,000 sq. ft.) accommodates up to 450 guests.
* **Why it’s the best:** The Gotham Ballroom is notable for being completely **column-free** with 20-foot ceilings and floor-to-ceiling windows, making sightlines perfect for presentations or galas. It offers a quieter, elevated luxury feel compared to the mega-convention hotels.

### 3. Best Major Corporate Alternative: **Sheraton New York Times Square Hotel**
A favorite for international conferences, political events, and major corporate summits.
* **Location:** 53rd Street & 7th Avenue (3 blocks north of Times Square)
* **Total Meeting Space:** Over 60,000 sq. ft. across 43 breakout rooms.
* **The Ballroom:** The **Metropolitan Ballroom** spans over 13,000 sq. ft. and can host up to 2,500 people.
* **Why it’s the best:** It sits slightly north of the heaviest tourist traffic, making arrival and departure easier for guests while still being an easy walk to Times Square. Its dedicated convention team is widely regarded as one of the best in the city.

### 4. Best Trendy & Modern Event Space: **Hard Rock Hotel New York**
If you want something brand new, stylish, and tech-forward rather than a traditional, formal hotel space.
* **Location:** 48th Street between 6th & 7th Avenues (1 block from Times Square)
* **Total Meeting Space:** Multiple flexible spaces, including high-tech boardrooms and music-centric venues.
* **The Event Space:** **The Venue on Music Row**—a stunning two-story, 6,000+ sq. ft. subterranean venue that holds up to 400 guests.

Hosting a product launch in the Times Square area gives you access to unmatched energy, world-class AV infrastructure, and high branding potential. 

To help you narrow down the options, here are the top venues in and around Times Square, categorized by event style, size, and vibe:

---

### 1. High-Tech & Immersive (Best for Tech, Consumer Electronics, & Digital Products)

*   **Lightbox** *(W 37th St, just south of Times Square)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Modern, fully customizable digital canvas.
    *   **Why it works:** Features 360-degree tech projection mapping, high-speed connectivity, and customizable walls. You can make the entire venue morph to fit your brand identity with the flip of a switch.
    *   **Capacity:** Up to 300 guests.

*   **The Glasshouse** *(W 48th St & 11th Ave – Midtown West)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Ultra-luxury, futuristic, massive scale.
    *   **Why it works:** If you are launching something massive (like an automotive product, major software enterprise, or global brand initiative), this is NYC’s premiere venue. It features floor-to-ceiling windows, outdoor terraces, heavy-duty freight elevators, and built-in production tech.
    *   **Capacity:** 100 to 1,850+ guests.

---

### 2. Trendy & Fashion-Forward (Best for Lifestyle, Beauty, & Media Launches)

*   **The Times Square EDITION** *(47th St & 7th Ave)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Boutique luxury, highly curated, stylish.
    *   **Why it works:** Offers versatile spaces like **The Paradise Club** (a performance-focused venue with advanced lighting) and an outdoor terrace overlooking Times Square. Excellent food and beverage program curated by Chef John Fraser.
    *   **Capacity:** 50 to 200 guests depending on the room/space used.

*   **Hard Rock Hotel New York** *(W 48th St)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Music-infused, sleek, vibrant.
    *   **Why it works:** **"The Venue on Music Row"** is a built-in event space with concert-grade sound, lighting, and stage capability. Perfect for a launch that includes a key performance, live demonstration, or VIP concert component.
    *   **Capacity:** Up to 400 standing / 200 seated.

---

### 3. Iconic Views & Rooftops (Best for Evening VIP Receptions & Photo Ops)

*   **St. Cloud at The Knickerbocker Hotel** *(42nd St & Broadway)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Upscale rooftop luxury directly over the heart of Times Square.
    *   **Why it works:** Offers three plush corner "skypods" that look straight down onto Times Square. Provides immediate, unmistakable NYC branding for press photos and social media content.
    *   **Capacity:** Up to 250 for a venue buyout.

*   **Dear Irving on Hudson** *(W 40th St)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Retro-chic cocktail lounge spanning the 40th and 41st floors of the Aliz Hotel.
    *   **Why it works:** Offers 360-degree views of Manhattan, high-end mixology, and a sophisticated atmosphere. Great for evening press launches or private influencer gatherings.
    *   **Capacity:** Up to 300 across both floors.

---

### 4. Large Corporate & High-Capacity Venues

*   **New York Marriott Marquis** *(Broadway between 45th & 46th)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Classic, massive, right in the center of the action.
    *   **Why it works:** Offers massive ballrooms and flexible breakout spaces. Crucially, they control major digital signage on Broadway, allowing you to bundle **billboard advertising directly outside** with your inside event.
    *   **Capacity:** 50 to 2,000+ guests.

*   **Sony Hall** *(W 46th St)*
    *   **The Vibe:** Historic yet tech-forward performance hall.
    *   **Why it works:** Operated by Blue Note, it features a 3D immersive audio system (Sony's Spatial Sound Technology), full-service catering, and a built-in stage setup for major keynote speeches or product reveals.
    *   **Capacity:** Up to 1,000 standing / 500 seated.

---

### Key Strategy: Digital Billboard Amplification
If you host an event in Times Square, consider buying a **15-to-30-minute billboard slot** (via companies like Silvercast or TSX Entertainment) right outside your venue during the event. You can stream your product launch live onto the street, bring guests outside for a "curtain drop" moment, or use it as a backdrop for press photos.

---

### Tips for Times Square Logistics:
1. **Load-in/Load-out:** Traffic around 42nd–50th Streets is notoriously slow. Ensure your venue has a dedicated loading dock (like *The Glasshouse* or *Marriott Marquis*) if you have heavy staging/tech.
2. **Security:** If you are inviting high-profile executives or celebrities, verify the venue’s VIP entrance and security protocols, as sidewalk crowd control in Times Square can be difficult.
3. **Accessibility:** Confirm proximity to Port Authority, Penn Station, or major subway lines (1, 2, 3, N, Q, R, W, A, C, E) to make attendance frictionless for local media.

When planning a trip to Manhattan for sightseeing and Broadway shows, staying in a centrally located area can enhance your experience. Here are some neighborhoods and hotel recommendations that could be ideal for your visit:

1. **Times Square/Theater District**:
   - **Why**: Proximity to Broadway theaters and the vibrant energy of Times Square.
   - **Hotels**: Consider the Marriott Marquis, The Knickerbocker, or The Chatwal.

2. **Midtown West**:
   - **Why**: Close to major attractions like Rockefeller Center, MoMA, and Central Park.
   - **Hotels**: The Hudson New York, The Warwick, or The London NYC.

3. **Midtown East**:
   - **Why**: Offers a quieter stay with easy access to Fifth Avenue shopping and the Chrysler Building.
   - **Hotels**: The Grand Hyatt, The New York Palace, or The Lexington Hotel.

4. **Hell’s Kitchen**:
   - **Why**: Known for its diverse dining options and proximity to Broadway without the hustle of Times Square.
   - **Hotels**: Ink 48 Hotel, YOTEL New York, or The Kimpton Ink48 Hotel.

5. **Upper West Side**:
   - **Why**: Offers a more residential feel with access to Central Park and Lincoln Center.
   - **Hotels**: The Empire Hotel, Hotel Beacon, or The Excelsior Hotel.

6. **Chelsea**:
   - **Why**: Known for its art galleries, trendy boutiques, and vibrant nightlife, with good subway connections.
   - **Hotels**: The High Line Hotel, The Standard, High Line, or The Maritime Hotel.

The best upscale hotel near Broadway depends slightly on whether you want to be **right in the heart of the action** or in a **quiet, ultra-luxury sanctuary** just a few blocks away. 

Here are the top luxury hotels near the Theater District, categorized by style:

---

### 1. **The Overall Best Pick: The Chatwal, a Luxury Collection Hotel**
* **Location:** 44th Street (between 5th and 6th Aves)
* **Vibe:** Art Deco Glamour, Intimate, Refined
* **Distance to Broadway:** 3–5 minute walk

**Why it’s the best:** 
The Chatwal strikes the absolute perfect balance. It is located on 44th Street—putting you steps away from major playhouses like the Belasco and the Hudson—yet it sits just far enough east of Times Square to avoid the chaotic crowds. Housed in a landmark 1930s building originally home to The Lambs (America’s first professional theater club), it embraces rich theatrical history. Expect personal butler service, plush suede walls, and the iconic *Lambs Club* restaurant.

---

### 2. **Best Modern Luxury: The Times Square EDITION**
* **Location:** 7th Avenue at 47th Street
* **Vibe:** Chic, Greenery-filled Oasis, High-Energy
* **Distance to Broadway:** 0-minute walk (In the heart of it)

**Why stay here:**

# Times Square Hotel Comparison for a 3-Night NYC Leisure Trip

## Quick Overview

| Hotel | Star Rating | Est. Price/Night | Best For |
|-------|-------------|------------------|----------|

  - Strong loyalty program (Bonvoy points)
  - Massive rooms by NYC standards
- **Cons:**
  - Can feel impersonal/convention-heavy
  - Noisy location (request high floors)
  - Pricey food & beverage on-site
- **3-Night Est. Total:** ~$1,050–$1,650

---

- **Location:** 42nd & Broadway
- **Pros:**
  - Stunning Beaux-Arts historic building (built 1906)
  - Rooftop bar with panoramic views
  - Smaller, boutique feel vs. mega-hotels
  - Excellent service-to-guest ratio
- **Cons:**
  - Premium price point
  - Smaller rooms
  - Limited on-site amenities vs. larger hotels
- **3-Night Est. Total:** ~$1,200–$1,950

---

- **Location:** 50th & 8th Ave (steps from Times Square)
- **Pros:**
  - Stylish, modern design
  - Excellent tech (mood lighting, smart TV control)
  - Great common/social spaces
  - Usually includes free WiFi
- **Cons:**
  - Rooms are small (by design)
  - No traditional room service
  - Not ideal for families with multiple people
- **3-Night Est. Total:** ~$540–$900

---

### 👨‍👩‍👧 Best for Families — **Novotel New York Times Square**
- **Location:** 52nd & Broadway
- **Pros:**
  - Kids under 16 eat free
  - Spacious family rooms available
  - Quieter block than mid-40s
  - Reliable Accor brand consistency
- **Cons:**
  - Less glamorous than competitors
  - Dated decor in some rooms
- **3-Night Est. Total:** ~$660–$1,140

---

### ✨ Best Boutique Luxury — **EDITION Times Square**
- **Location:** 46th & Broadway
- **Pros:**
  - Ian Schrager-designed (stunning interiors)
  - Exceptional restaurant & bar scene
  - Feels exclusive despite central location
  - Rooftop access
- **Cons:**
  - Very expensive
  - Style may overshadow comfort for some
- **3-Night Est. Total:** ~$1,500–$2,700

---

## Key Decision Factors

### 📍 Location Tips
> Times Square sits between **42nd–53rd St & 7th–8th Ave**
- **42nd–47th St** = Most "in it" — maximum buzz, maximum noise
- **48th–53rd St** = Slightly quieter, still walkable to everything
- **High floors** = Essential for noise reduction anywhere here

### 🔊 Noise Considerations
- Times Square **never fully quiets** — bring earplugs or request high floors
- North-facing rooms typically quieter than street-facing
- All hotels have decent soundproofing, but light sleepers should note this

### 🚇 Transit Access
All options are near:
- **N/Q/R/W, 1/2/3, A/C/E** subway lines
- Walking distance to Broadway theaters, Central Park, MoMA, Rockefeller Center

---

| You Are... | Best Pick |
|------------|-----------|
| First-time NYC visitor | Marriott Marquis |
| Couple on a romantic trip | Knickerbocker or EDITION |
| Budget-savvy traveler | citizenM |
| Family with kids | Novotel |
| Points maximizer | Marriott Marquis (Bonvoy) or Renaissance |
| Luxury splurger | EDITION Times Square |

---

## 💡 Pro Tips for Booking
- **Book directly** with the hotel for best cancellation policies
- **Thursday–Sunday** are typically pricier than Mon–Wed
- **Check hotel + show packages** — many partner with Broadway theaters
- Prices **spike significantly** during holidays, New Year's Eve, and school breaks
- Consider **Midtown West alternatives** (Hell's Kitchen area) for 10–20% savings

---

*Prices are estimates and fluctuate based on season and demand. Always verify current rates on hotel websites or booking platforms.*

For a Broadway date night with rooftop cocktails, stay in **Midtown’s Theater District or just south near Bryant Park**. You’ll be within walking distance of most theaters, avoiding a late-night subway or taxi ride after the show.[1]

### Best hotel picks

- **Hard Rock Hotel New York** — Best overall for convenience and atmosphere. It’s near Broadway and has **RT60 Rooftop Bar & Lounge**, 34 floors up, serving cocktails, bites, and city views.[10]
- **Moxy NYC Times Square** — Best for a lively, youthful date. Its rooftop, **Magic Hour**, is an indoor/outdoor bar with skyline views and a playful atmosphere.[7]
- **Refinery Hotel** — Best for a stylish, more romantic feel. The hotel has a rooftop bar and an intimate industrial-chic design; many rooms offer Empire State Building views.[7]
- **Archer Hotel New York** — Best for a boutique stay with a polished rooftop. **Spyglass** offers panoramic views and is close to Broadway, Bryant Park, and Grand Central.[7]
- **Margaritaville Resort Times Square** — Best for maximum proximity and a casual rooftop night. Its **5 o’Clock Somewhere Rooftop Bar** has cocktails, frozen margaritas, shareable food, and Midtown views.[1]
- **Tempo by Hilton New York Times Square** — Best for pre-show cocktails. **Highball**, on Level Eleven, serves cocktails and shareable plates with panoramic views before the short walk to Broadway.[4]

### Recommended date-night plan

1. Stay at **Hard Rock**, **Refinery**, or **Archer**.
2. Have sunset cocktails at the hotel rooftop.
3. Walk 5–15 minutes to the theater.
4. After the show, reserve a quieter nightcap at **Bar 54**, **St. Cloud**, or another nearby rooftop; Broadway performances commonly end around 9:30–10:30 p.m.[1]

**Top recommendation:** Choose **Hard Rock Hotel New York** for the easiest all-in-one evening, or **Refinery Hotel** if you want a more romantic and sophisticated atmosphere. Reserve rooftop seating in advance, especially for Friday and Saturday nights.

Traveling to NYC with teenagers requires a balance: you want to be in the middle of the excitement, but you also need **larger-than-average rooms, strong Wi-Fi, full-service amenities (concierge, room service, luggage holding), and good soundproofing** so everyone actually sleeps.

Here are the top full-service hotels in and around Times Square that hit the sweet spot for families with teens:

---

### 1. Hard Rock Hotel New York
**Best For:** Overall teen appeal, cool factor, and modern tech.
* **Location:** 159 W 48th St (Just off Times Square, steps from Rockefeller Center)
* **Why Teens Love It:** It feels trendy and exclusive. Rooms feature Fender guitar rentals, Crosley record players, floor-to-ceiling windows, and high-tech room controls. The lobby and public spaces are filled with modern music memorabilia (hip-hop, pop, and classic rock).
* **Why Parents Love It:** Excellent full-service standards, fantastic soundproofing, and a location that is *just* far enough off Broadway to avoid the worst of the pedestrian gridlock. 
* **Amenities:** 24-hour room service, full concierge, upscale dining (Sessions), and RT60 rooftop lounge (accessible to families earlier in the evening).

---

### 2. New York Marriott Marquis
**Best For:** The iconic "in the heart of it all" Times Square experience.
* **Location:** 1535 Broadway (Right on the main strip)
* **Why Teens Love It:** The dramatic 49-story atrium with iconic glass elevators is a huge hit. It places them directly above the glowing billboards and Broadway theaters.
* **Why Parents Love It:** It is a massive, highly efficient full-service machine. The rooms are **some of the largest standard hotel rooms in Times Square**, which is a huge deal when sharing space with teens. 
* **Amenities:** Multiple full-service restaurants, a massive gym overlooking Times Square, theatrical ticket desk, concierge, and expansive lobby space to sit and relax outside the room.

---

### 3. Hyatt Centric Times Square New York
**Best For:** Spacious layout, great views, and a slightly quieter feel.
* **Location:** 135 W 45th St (Half a block from Times Square)
* **Why Teens Love It:** Floor-to-ceiling windows with incredible city views, sleek modern design, and fast Wi-Fi. 
* **Why Parents Love It:** Located on a quieter side street, giving you instant access to the action without stepping out directly into crowds. They offer **guaranteed connecting rooms** (must book directly or request early), which is ideal if you want separate space from your teens.
* **Amenities:** Full concierge service, dry cleaning, on-site restaurant (T45 Market), 24-hour fitness center, and Bar 54 (NYC’s highest open-air hotel rooftop bar—great for family photos before 7 PM).

---

### 4. The Westin New York at Times Square
**Best For:** Room space, family comfort, and subway access.
* **Location:** 270 W 43rd St (At 8th Avenue)
* **Why Teens Love It:** Connected directly to the E-Walk complex (which includes movie theaters and food options). It’s also very close to major subway hubs (A/C/E/1/2/3/N/Q/R lines), making independent exploration easy.
* **Why Parents Love It:** Famous "Heavenly Beds" and "Heavenly Baths" (great after walking 10 miles a day). They offer generous **Family Suites** and double-queen layouts.
* **Amenities:** 24-hour room service, full concierge desk, Foundry Kitchen & Bar, and WestinWORKOUT Fitness Studio.

---

### 5. Margaritaville Resort Times Square
**Best For:** Summer/spring trips and a unique resort vibe.
* **Location:** 560 7th Ave ( corner of 40th & 7th)
* **Why Teens Love It:** **It has the only outdoor heated pool in Times Square.** After a long morning of sightseeing, teens love coming back to swim with a view of the skyscrapers. 
* **Why Parents Love It:** Despite the fun/island theme, it is a brand-new building (opened 2021) with top-notch infrastructure, quiet glass, and clean, bright rooms.
* **Amenities:** Outdoor pool, multiple on-site dining options, room service, fitness center, and vibrant common areas.

---

### Family Booking Tips for NYC with Teens:
1. **Request High Floors:** Always ask for a room on the 15th floor or higher. It significantly reduces street noise (sirens, honking, construction).
2. **Double Queen vs. Two Doubles:** Many NYC hotels feature "Double/Double" beds (full size). If your teens are tall, specifically look for hotels offering **Two Queen Beds** (like the *Westin* or *Marriott Marquis*).
3. **Broadway Tickets:** Use the hotel concierge as soon as you check in. They often have access to house seats or can help navigate the best times to hit the TKTS booth.

While staying directly in Times Square is exciting, the best family-friendly hotels are usually located **1 to 2 blocks off the main pedestrian plaza**. This gives you instant access to Broadway shows and lights, but provides a quieter environment when it’s time for the kids to sleep.

Here are the top family-friendly hotels in and around Times Square, categorized by what they do best:

---

### 1. Best Overall for Kids: **Margaritaville Resort Times Square**
* **Location:** 7th Ave & 40th St (1 block from main Times Square)
* **Why Families Love It:** It features a **heated outdoor pool** (open year-round), which is extremely rare in Times Square and a massive hit with kids. 
* **Key Perks:** 
  * Surprisingly excellent soundproofing (virtually no street noise makes it to the rooms).
  * Fun, colorful design that feels like a vacation within a vacation.
  * On-site dining options that are very kid-pleasing.

### 2. Best for Extra Space & Budget: **Residence Inn New York Manhattan/Times Square**
* **Location:** 39th St & 6th Ave (2 blocks from Times Square, across from Bryant Park)
* **Why Families Love It:** NYC hotel rooms are notoriously tiny, but this hotel offers **suite-style layouts with kitchenettes** (microwave, mini-fridge, sink).
* **Key Perks:**
  * **Free hot breakfast included daily** (saves a family of four $80–$100 a day in NYC).
  * Kitchenettes allow you to store snacks and easy meals for toddler melt-down moments.
  * Located right next to Bryant Park, giving kids a green space to run around.

### 3. Best for Large Families (5+ People): **TRYP by Wyndham Times Square South**
* **Location:** 35th St between 8th & 9th Ave (10-minute walk to Times Square)
* **Why Families Love It:** They offer specialized **Family Rooms featuring bunk beds**, two double beds, and sleeper sofas that can comfortably sleep 6 to 8 people in one room.
* **Key Perks:**
  * Very spacious room configurations rarely found in Manhattan.
  * Family suites feature two bathrooms (a major sanity-saver).
  * Slightly removed from the main Times Square crush, making street navigation easier with strollers.

### 4. Best Classic Hotel Experience: **The Westin New York at Times Square**
* **Location:** 42nd St & 8th Ave (1 block from Times Square)
* **Why Families Love It:** It offers a polished, high-end hotel feel with spacious double-queen rooms and exceptional service.
* **Key Perks:**
  * Direct indoor access to the 42nd St Subway Station (no walking through rain or snow to catch a train).
  * Highly rated for clean, comfortable beds ("Heavenly Beds") and quiet, thick windows.
  * Very close to major Broadway theaters like *The Lion King* and *Aladdin*.

---

### Pro-Tips for Families Staying in Times Square:

1. **Request a High Floor:** Always ask for a room on the 10th floor or higher to minimize street noise, siren sounds, and neon light bleed.
2. **Beware of "Destination Fees":** Almost every hotel in Times Square charges a daily "Resort/Facility Fee" ($30–$50/night). Make sure to factor this into your budget and check if it includes food/beverage credits you can use.
3. **Don’t Eat on 7th Ave/Broadway:** Avoid eating at the big chain restaurants right in the center of Times Square—they mark up prices significantly. Walk two blocks west to **9th Avenue (Hell’s Kitchen)** for incredible, family-friendly, and reasonably priced pizza, burgers, and international food.
